chunks: Sa'eed al-A'raj narrated to us saying: I and Sulayman ibn Khalid went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he initiated [the conversation], saying: 'O Sulayman! Whatever has come from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), take with it, and whatever he forbade, refrain from it. The merit that flowed for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed for him, and for the Messenger of Allah is the merit over all of Allah's creation. One who finds fault with Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) regarding anything from his rulings is like one who finds fault with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and with His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And one who rejects him in something small or large is on the boundary of shirk with Allah.

'O Sulayman! Whatever has come from Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), take with it, and whatever he forbade, refrain from it. The merit that flowed for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) flowed for him, and for the Messenger of Allah is the merit over all of Allah's creation. One who finds fault with Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) regarding anything from his rulings is like one who finds fault with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and with His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family). And one who rejects him in something small or large is on the boundary of shirk with Allah.

Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of Allah be upon him) was Allah's Door that cannot be accessed except through it, and His Way, such that whoever travels by other than it will perish. And by that, the Imams (peace be upon them) proceeded, one after another. Allah made them the pillars of the earth lest it shake with its inhabitants, and His conclusive proof upon those above the earth and those beneath the soil.

Then he said: 'Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: I am Allah's Distributor between Paradise and the Fire, I am the Great Differentiator, and I am the owner of the staff and the branding iron. All of the angels and the Spirit have acknowledged for me the likes of what they acknowledged for Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). And I have been loaded with the likes of Muhammad's burden (peace be upon him and his family), and it is the Lord's burden.

And Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) will be called, then clothed and made to speak; and I will be called, then clothed and made to speak, and I shall speak in accordance with his manner of speech. I have been given qualities that no one before me was given: I was taught the knowledge of deaths, tribulations, lineages, and the decisive word. Nothing that preceded me has escaped me, and nothing that is hidden from me eludes me. I give glad tidings by the permission of Allah, and I fulfill from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic — all of that is what Allah has enabled me in, by His permission.'

key_terms.أَرْكَانُ الْأَرْضِ: Pillars of the earth — the Imams as cosmic stabilizers preventing the earth from shaking
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ الْبَالِغَةُ: The conclusive proof — the Imams as God's definitive argument over all creation
key_terms.الْفَارُوقُ الْأَكْبَرُ: The Great Differentiator — one who distinguishes truth from falsehood
key_terms.الْمِيسَمُ: The branding iron — a symbol of eschatological authority to mark and identify people
key_terms.بَابُ اللَّهِ: Allah's Door — a title for Imam Ali indicating that access to divine guidance is only through him
key_terms.حَمُولَةُ الرَّبِّ: The Lord's burden — the divine trust of prophethood/imamate
key_terms.فَصْلُ الْخِطَابِ: The decisive word — the capacity for final authoritative judgment
key_terms.قَسِيمُ اللَّهِ: Allah's Distributor — Ali's claim to be the one who assigns people to paradise or hellfire on Judgment Day

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the authority and qualities of Imam Ali in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) teaches his companions Sa'eed al-A'raj and Sulayman ibn Khalid about the divine authority of Amir al-Mu'minin (Imam Ali, peace be upon him). The Imam establishes that Ali's authority is identical to that of the Prophet — his commands and prohibitions carry the same binding force, and to oppose them is equivalent to shirk. He further reports Ali's own words, in which Ali claims extraordinary gifts: being the distributor of paradise and hellfire, the owner of the staff and branding iron of eschatological judgment, and possessing knowledge of deaths, tribulations, genealogies, and the decisive word. This hadith is central to the Shia doctrine of imamate, asserting both the cosmic function of the Imams as stabilizers of the earth and their status as conclusive proofs of God upon all of creation.
